summary: Implemented the correctness-first Gemma 4 MLX cache bridge: public gemma4 and gemma4_text models retain complete per-request mlx-lm cache lists, including the 35-layer/15-owned-cache YOCO shape; radix caching, overlap scheduling, and chunked prefill fail at startup with actionable flags; the default native-cache scheduler budget is conservatively limited to 2,048 tokens. Portable policy tests pass, but this Linux x86_64/ROCm node cannot execute MLX/Metal or load the Apple Silicon E2B checkpoint, so the candidate is not claimed as fully fixed.

tests.what_was_measured: Portable recognition and adversarial configuration policy: public wrapper/text backbone detection, complete reporting of all unsafe scheduler flags, and acceptance of the conservative configuration. Result: 3 passed.

MLX-gated regression coverage includes the real Gemma 4 35-layer/15-cache ownership shape, independent cache mutation for two requests, and request-finish release. Result: 43 skipped because mlx is unavailable on this non-Apple host; this is retained as blocker evidence, not a functional pass.
Python syntax/import compilation for the changed MLX backend and tests.

gpu_execution_evidence: Prepared node is Linux 4.18 x86_64 with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2; importlib reports mlx=None and mlx_lm=None. MLX requires Apple Silicon/Metal, so no qualified GPU numerical reference was possible.
remaining_limitations: No Apple Silicon or Metal device was available; the public gemma4.Model wrapper and tiny real architecture could not be instantiated here.
mlx-community/gemma-4-e2b-it-4bit was not downloaded or launched, and /v1/chat/completions was not exercised.
Greedy output was not compared token-for-token with unmodified mlx-lm across a prompt longer than the synthetic sliding window.
The MLX-gated cache isolation and 35-layer/15-cache regression tests are present but skipped on this host.

Only the E2B text correctness bridge is targeted. Radix/prefix reuse, overlap/chained decode, chunked prefill, fused batched attention, long-context claims, Gemma 4 Unified, E4B/31B/26B, multimodal inputs, MTP, and custom Gemma-specific Metal kernels remain unimplemented or unverified.
No native C++ or FlyDSL code changed; native rebuild requirements are not applicable to this contribution.
